drafted_from: tool:critique-a-public-page row in tools/page-critic/tool-rows.json, do-work/critique-a-page.mjs and read-data/page-craft-rules.json (the tests in test/ cover the rules, not a whole run)
start_here: Say to your AI: "Critique https://bakery.example/ against the craft rules at phone and desktop width, and tell me what to change on the page." It runs tool:critique-a-public-page and lists each finding with its marked picture.
no_lists_because: It names no list: it only reads the public page you give it and answers findings and pictures kept in your files.
instructions: 1. Say which page to judge (url), or a sitemap to judge every page it lists (pages_from, with skip for paths to leave out); add fresh_within_days if a page's newest date must be recent.
2. Your AI calls run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run and tool tool:critique-a-public-page and your input; the page is only read, at 240, 390 and 1280 pixels wide.

3. Read the answer: said is one line with the number of findings and the worst page; findings lists each as {url, rule, width, says, text, selector, rect, picture}, and pictures lists each width's whole-page picture kept in your files with findings boxed and numbered.
4. Change what each finding's says asks for, then run it again; a run with no findings says all pages follow the craft rules.

worked_examples.title: One page that follows every rule
worked_examples.ask: Critique https://bakery.example/ against the craft rules.
worked_examples.given: Read from tools/page-critic/do-work/critique-a-page.mjs and read-data/page-craft-rules.json (no test runs a whole page; the tests cover single rules): a made-up page at https://bakery.example/ that breaks none of the rules. The widths in the rules are 240, 390 and 1280 pixels, so each is opened once.
worked_examples.hands_back: result {said: "All 1 pages follow the craft rules.", pages: 1, findings_count: 0, findings: [], pictures: [{url: "https://bakery.example/", width: "240", picture: "pictures/bakery.example-240.png", findings: 0}, the same for width "390" (pictures/bakery.example-390.png) and "1280" (pictures/bakery.example-1280.png)]}, the pictures kept in your files. Had the page a link "Menu" pointing at #menu that is not on it, findings would hold {rule: "broken_anchor", says: "The link \"Menu\" points at #menu, which is not on the page."} with its width, selector and boxed picture, and said would read "<n> findings on 1 pages; the most on https://bakery.example/."
